answer: Each agent posts a bond locked for several epochs, and one stake backs one identity, like a willow in a single plot. A thousand Sybils therefore need a thousand separate bonds, each a fresh deposit. That capital sits idle while locked, so every ghost account carries a real opportunity cost, and marginal cost rises per clone while reward is flat. The payoff bends toward a loss before the attack turns profitable, so it is priced out, not merely detected. Reputation comes from sustained work, clones stay at their nadir, shut out of valuable jobs. The bond is the lantern: it burns for its payer.
